title: "Wine Quality & Climate Change"
---

## Project description

*(placeholder — replace with your own project description)*

This project explores two questions: what shapes wine quality and pricing
across regions, reviewers, and varieties, and whether there is any visible
relationship between long-run global CO2 emissions and where high-quality
wine is produced.

## Motivating questions

*(placeholder — refine or replace)*

- Which regions and reviewers stand out in the wine tasting data, and why?
- Is there a relationship between a wine's rating and its price?
- As cumulative CO2 emissions have grown, has the geography of
  high-scoring wine production shifted?

## Data sources

*(placeholder — add citations/links once finalized)*

- **Wine tasting reviews**: `data/winemag-data-130k-v2.csv` — ~130,000 wine
  reviews with country, province, region, variety, price, points, reviewer,
  and a free-text tasting description.
- **CO2 emissions**: `data/CO2+Emissions/visualizing_global_co2_data.csv` —
  a country-year panel of CO2 emissions and related indicators, 1750–2021.

## How to navigate this site

*(placeholder)*

- **Wine quality in the world** — descriptive analysis of the wine reviews:
  pricing by province, the points/price relationship, reviewer
  specialization, and common language in positive vs. negative reviews.
- **Best wine searcher** — an interactive map to find top-rated and
  best value-for-money wines by country, plus a filterable data table.
- **Global warming and wine** — an exploration of cumulative CO2 emissions
  over time alongside wine quality and production latitude.
